title: Nuevo Laredo zoo opens 'Monarcas en Vuelo' stand to teach families about monarch migration
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo's zoo is hosting an informational stand about the monarch butterfly migration on November weekends, inviting families to learn how to protect the species as it passes through the border city on its way to central Mexico.
content:
Nuevo Laredo's zoo is turning into a classroom for monarch butterflies. The Zoológico de Nuevo Laredo has installed an informational stand called “Monarcas en Vuelo,” inviting families to learn about the monarch migration as the butterflies pass through the border city, according to Desde Donde Estamos.

The stand is an initiative of the municipal government of Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, organized through the city's Coordinación General de Gestión Ambiental. It is part of the city's observance of the Día de la Mariposa Monarca and the fall migration season, the report said.

Each fall, monarch butterflies travel thousands of kilometers from Canada and the United States to the forests of Michoacán and the State of Mexico, and Nuevo Laredo sits along their migratory route. The stand teaches visitors about the monarchs' history and their long journey, the threats they face — including habitat loss, insecticide use and climate change — and what residents can do from their own homes and neighborhoods to help them along the way, including protecting green spaces, native plants and pollinator gardens, according to the report.

The stand will be open on November weekends from noon to 6 p.m.: November 14 and 15, November 21 and 22, and November 28 and 29. The city is inviting children, young people and adults to visit as a family and learn more about the region's biodiversity, the report said.

Sources: Desde Donde Estamos, Nov. 12, 2026.
